Learn More Meet Congresswoman Lois Frankel Congresswoman Lois Frankel has dedicated her life to public service, championing the needs of Palm Beach County residents as a state legislator, mayor, and now in her seventh term in Congress. A proud “working grandmother,” Lois brings her passion for family and community to her work every day. LEARN MORE   Key Issues Lower Costs So families can comfortably afford groceries, gas, housing, and prescription drugs. Social Security and Medicare So our loved ones can age with comfort and dignity. Health Care So everyone can access affordable, quality health care. Reproductive Freedom So women can access the health care they need, including legal abortion, contraception, and IVF. Child and Long-term Care So families can access quality, affordable care for their children and older loved ones. We need to bring costs down at the grocery store, gas station, and pharmacy, so no one struggles to meet their most basic needs. I am committed to lowering the cost of living and making essentials like groceries, gas, and prescription drugs more affordable. Social Security and Medicare | U.S. Representative Lois Frankel Palm Beach County is home to over 350,000 seniors. I will always fight to protect Social Security and Medicare, lower the costs of prescription drugs, and reduce falls among older adults. </p> <h2 style="font-size: 1.8rem;">Social Security</h2> <p> Social Security is not a handout. For the more than 380,000 seniors in Palm Beach County, it is a promise that they have earned through a lifetime of hard work. I am proud to support bills like the <em>Social Security 2100 Act</em>, which would increase benefits for retirees, protect against inflation, support low-wage workers, reduce Social Security taxes for lower- and middle-income earners, provide caregiver credits, strengthen the Social Security Trust Fund, and more. I will always oppose Republicans’ efforts to privatize Social Security or cut the essential benefits that our seniors have earned, and I continue to speak out against the Trump Administration’s efforts to gut the agency and customer service. </p> <h2 style="font-size: 1.8rem;">Medicare</h2> <p><br /> In 2022, Congress passed and President Biden signed into law the <em><a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/5376/text">Inflation Reduction Act</a></em>, which lowered drug prices by allowing Medicare to negotiate fairer prices on behalf of seniors, capping out-of-pocket costs for Medicare beneficiaries, and penalizing drug companies that raise prices faster than the rate of inflation. I also support legislation to lower the Medicare eligibility age, reduce premiums, expand benefits, and provide dental, hearing, and vision coverage. I will oppose any efforts by the Trump Administration to reverse these cost saving initiatives. </p> <h2 style="font-size: 1.8rem;">Falls Prevention</h2> <p> Falls are the leading cause of injury and injury-related deaths among adults over 65. As the founder of the Bipartisan Task Force on Falls Prevention, I have worked with colleagues across the aisle to address the epidemic of elderly falls. Reproductive Freedom | U.S. Representative Lois Frankel I believe that women, not politicians, should decide whether and when to start or grow a family. That means women should have access to the reproductive health care services they need, including abortion. Since the Trump-appointed Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, over 20 states, including Florida, have banned or severely restricted abortion access. Women in Florida are now living under a cruel 6-week ban, before most women even know they are pregnant.</p> <p dir="ltr"><br /> I am fully committed to restoring the right to abortion nationwide. That’s why I am proud to co-lead the <em><a href="https://frankel.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=4879">Women’s Health Protection Act</a></em>, which would establish women’s rights to abortion care and doctors’ rights to provide that care without the threat of being sued or going to prison. Child and Long-Term Care | U.S. Representative Lois Frankel As a working grandmother, I have seen firsthand the skyrocketing prices of child care and long-term care. Child care has become completely inaccessible for too many families. Meanwhile, about 3 million Americans provide unpaid caregiving to an aging, sick, or disabled relative, costing our economy $600 billion a year. I am committed to ensuring families can access quality, affordable care for their children and their families. </p> <p> I have been proud to support legislation that would expand access to child care and long-term care, including the <em><a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/2976/cosponsors?s=2&amp;r=2&amp;q=%7B%22search%22%3A%22Child+Care+for+Working+Families+Act%22%7D" target="_blank">Child Care for Working Families Act</a></em>, which would cap child care costs at 7 percent of a family’s income and ensure child care workers are paid a living wage, and the <em><a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/547/cosponsors" target="_blank">Better Care Better Jobs Act</a></em>, which would expand access to long-term care for older adults and Americans with disabilities. </p> <p> As a Member of the House Appropriations Committee, I have fought for increased funding for child care programs, including the <em>Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG)</em> and <em>Head Start, and Home and Community-Based Services</em>, which help seniors and individuals with disabilities live dignified lives in the setting of their choice, including in their own homes.</p>" /> Skip to Content Child and Long-Term Care Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email As a working grandmother, I have seen firsthand the skyrocketing prices of child care and long-term care. Israel and Antisemitism | U.S. Representative Lois Frankel <strong>ISRAEL</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">I will always stand by Israel, and I am committed to ensuring our ally has the resources and support needed to defend itself and maintain peace and security. In Congress, as Ranking Member of the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Subcommittee, I support continued security assistance to Israel and robust funding for Israel’s missile defense capabilities. Since Hamas’s deadly attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, I have supported emergency aid to Israel as it works to dismantle Hamas and fight proxies on multiple fronts.</p> <p dir="ltr">I frequently meet with released hostages who were held in Gaza as well as their families, and will continue to speak out for the unconditional and immediate release of the remaining hostages.</p> <p dir="ltr">As part of that commitment to peace and security, I have consistently spoken out on the existential threat posed by Iran’s nuclear ambitions. For decades, the Iranian regime has armed terrorist proxies, called for the destruction of Israel and the United States, and relentlessly pursued nuclear weapons. It is vital that President Trump and Congress work together in a constructive, bipartisan manner to ensure Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon. The safety of Israel, our allies, and the United States depends on it.</p> <p dir="ltr"><strong>ANTISEMITISM</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">I am alarmed by the disturbing rise in antisemitism across our country, especially as a member of the Jewish community. I proudly serve on the Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, which aims to ensure Congress plays an integral role in condemning antisemitism and spearheading initiatives that promote tolerance worldwide. As a member of the Appropriations Committee, I have advocated for increased funding for security for synagogues and other places of worship that could be targets for hate crimes. Gun Violence Prevention | U.S. Representative Lois Frankel As a grandmother, I believe no parent or grandparent should fear for their child’s safety at school, the movies, or the grocery store. That’s why I have supported several policies to keep our communities safe from gun violence. </p> <p> In 2022, Congress passed and President Biden signed into law the <em><a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/senate-bill/2938/text" target="_blank">Bipartisan Safer Communities Act</a></em>, which addresses gun violence by keeping guns out of the hands of individuals under 21, helping the Department of Justice prosecute firearms traffickers, investing in mental health services, and closing loopholes that previously allowed domestic violence offenders to access firearms. </p> <p> As a member of the <em>Gun Violence Prevention Task Force</em>, I will continue to fight for further legislation to reduce gun violence, including measures to require safe storage of firearms, require universal background checks, create an Office of Gun Violence Prevention, prohibit “ghost guns” (guns without serial numbers), ban assault weapons and high capacity magazines, eliminate gun manufacturers’ liability immunity, and establish federal extreme risk protection orders (“red flag laws”). </p>" /> Skip to Content Gun Violence Prevention Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email As a grandmother, I believe no parent or grandparent should fear for their child’s safety at school, the movies, or the grocery store. Veterans and Servicemembers | U.S. Representative Lois Frankel As both the daughter and mother of Veterans, I will always advocate for the rights and benefits our servicemembers and Veterans deserve.</p> <p dir="ltr">I believe we must continue to improve services and resources for our Veterans, including access to health care, education, housing, and workforce training. That’s why in 2022, Congress passed and President Biden signed into law the <em><a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/3967/cosponsors">Honoring Our PACT Act</a></em>, which expanded eligibility for Veterans Administration (VA) health care benefits to Veterans exposed to burn pits, Agent Orange, and other toxic substances. I am also proud to sponsor the bipartisan <em><a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/1078/text">Veteran Education Empowerment Act</a></em>, which would authorize <a href="https://www.ed.gov/grants-and-programs/grants-higher-education/improvement-of-postsecondary-education/centers-of-excellence-veteran-student-success">Centers of Excellence for Veteran Student Success</a> at universities and colleges across the country, helping student Veterans transition from military to student life. Through this program, we have provided nearly $50 million in grants to over 100 schools since 2015, including Florida International University, so campuses can better serve student Veterans.</p> <p dir="ltr">This Congress, I have fervently pushed back against Republicans' Big Ugly Bill, to protect Medicaid and SNAP benefits for Veterans and to ensure that all women Veterans have the right to decide when and how to start a family.</p> <p dir="ltr">As a Member of the House Appropriations Committee, each year I fight for increased funding for health care and workforce training for Veterans, as well as assistance for Veterans suffering from homelessness. Health Care | U.S. Representative Lois Frankel I believe all Americans deserve access to affordable, quality health care, and I am fighting back hard against Republicans’ efforts to rip away health care for millions of families. For far too long, America’s health care system has been too expensive for many hardworking families and individuals. In 2010, Congress passed the <em><a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/111th-congress/house-bill/3590">Affordable Care Act</a></em> (ACA) to lower costs and provide quality health care to all Americans. Millions of people rely on the protections and benefits that this legislation provides, including prohibiting insurance companies from denying insurance for individuals with pre-existing conditions or dropping coverage when people get sick. Florida leads the nation in signups through the ACA insurance marketplace, with over 4.5 million Floridians enrolled in affordable health care through the marketplace in 2025.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">Since I’ve been in Congress, I have continued to work to improve and strengthen the ACA to make coverage accessible for even more Americans. In 2021, Congressional Democrats passed the <a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/1319/text">American Rescue Plan</a>, which allowed an additional 6 million Americans to enroll in affordable health care through the ACA, 80 percent of whom enrolled for under $10 per month. In 2022, we extended these benefits through 2025 with the passage of President Biden’s <em><a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/5376/text">Inflation Reduction Act</a></em> (IRA). The IRA also capped insulin at $35 per month for seniors on Medicare, capped seniors’ annual out-of-pocket drug spending, ensured free vaccines for Medicare beneficiaries, and allowed Medicare to negotiate lower drug prices for the first time.</p> <p dir="ltr">Unfortunately, due to Trump and Republicans’ Big, Ugly Law, vital ACA aid is set to expire at the end of this year.
